name: Two Plus One Poker
description: Guts-style poker variant. Each player is dealt two cards; players declare in or out; those who are in receive a third card. Hands rank as in Three-card Guts (three of a kind, straight flush, straight, flush, pair, nothing). Losers who stayed in match the pot.

history.origins: Guts-style match-pot poker variant. Each player dealt two cards, declare in or out, those in receive a third card; hands rank as Three-card Guts.
timeline: 20th century: Guts-style poker variant in American home games; two cards, declare in or out, then third card to those in; losers match the pot.
history.cultural: Played as a dealer's choice option in American home poker games.
history.evolution: Variant of Guts with a second deal: two cards then declare, then one card to those in; uses three-card hand ranking.

setup.dealing: Two cards face down to each player, one at a time. After declarations, one card to each player who declared in.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best three-card hand among players who declare in, or be the only player to declare in.
rules.gameplay: If the pot is empty all players ante. Dealer deals two cards face down to each player. Players declare in (compete for the pot) or out (drop out; no extra loss). Each player who declared in receives one more card face down. If more than one stayed in, they show hands and the best three-card hand wins the pot. All players who stayed in but did not win each pay an amount equal to the whole pot into the next deal. If only one stays in, that player takes the pot without showing.
keyRules: Two cards each face down; declare in or out (turn or simultaneous e.g. chips in fist); one card dealt to each player who is in; three-card Guts ranking: three of a kind, straight flush, straight, flush, pair, nothing; losers who stayed in each match the pot; agree ante and optional max loss per deal before play.

strategy.basic: Only declare in with a hand that has three-card potential (pair or draw to straight/flush).
strategy.intermediate: Consider pot size versus risk of matching; going in with weak two cards risks a big loss when you receive a bad third card.
strategy.advanced: In optional second-declare variant, staying in for the third card but then dropping loses only the extra ante, not the full pot match.
tips: Agree ante and maximum loss per deal before play.
Simultaneous declare (e.g. chips in fist) removes bluffing; turn order allows some bluffing.

variations.name: Second declare with extra ante
variations.description: Those who stay in for a third card pay an extra ante and take part in a second round of declaring in or out when they have three cards. Players who stay in for the third card but drop out after seeing it lose the extra ante but do not risk matching the pot.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Second-declare variant has no engine constant overrides; add when implementing optional second declare phase.
